protocol.title: High-throughput co-culture system for analysis of spatiotemporal cell-cell signaling
protocol.platform: Two-layer PDMS microfluidics (pneumatic valve control, 192-chamber array)
cell_lines: RelA-/- RelA-DsRed NIH3T3 mouse embryonic fibroblasts (3T3s)
Primary murine adult fibroblasts (RelA-YFP knock-in mouse)
protocol.objective: Automated high-throughput spatiotemporal co-culture platform enabling macrophage stimulation, cytokine gradient formation, live NF-kB single-cell imaging, spatially resolved cell retrieval, and downstream gene expression quantification at 192-chamber scale

device.fabrication: Conventional soft lithography; two-layer PDMS bonded to glass substrate (127.8 x 85.5 x 1 mm, Marienfeld); oxygen plasma bonding (Harrick, PDC-001)
layers: Fluid layer: thin PDMS ~50 um height, spun at 2300 RPM from ~10 g mixture on fluid mold pretreated with chlorotrimethylsilane
Control layer: thick PDMS slab with pneumatic valve features; aligned to fluid layer under custom stereomicroscope with XYZ translation stage

chambers.unit_structure: Pre-chamber (source) + receiving chamber partitioned into near/mid/far regions

valves.actuation: Solenoid valves (Festo, 197334) via Tygon tubes (Cole-Parmer, ND-100-80)

sink_channel.location: Bottom of receiving chamber, separated by pillar forest
sink_channel.function: Peristaltic pumping removes cytokines at far end; mimics capillary clearance
sink_channel.pumping: Gentle peristaltic; shear-free across multiple chambers simultaneously

imaging.environmental_control: Temperature, CO2, and humidity controlled enclosure
imaging.nfkb_quantification: Nucleus/cytosol DsRed intensity ratio per cell (Kudo et al., 2018 method)

reagents.fibroblast_media: DMEM high glucose (Gibco) + 10% FBS (Omega Scientific) + 2 mM GlutaMAX (Gibco) + 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Lonza)
reagents.fibronectin: Sigma-Aldrich FC010; chamber coating prior to cell loading
reagents.lps_high_dose: 50 ng/mL LPS (InvivoGen, tlrl-3pelps); macrophage stimulation in pre-chamber, 10 min
reagents.lps_low_dose: 3 ng/mL LPS; used in cell-patterning experiments (subthreshold for direct fibroblast activation)
reagents.tnf_alpha: 30 ng/mL TNF-a (R&D Systems, aa80-235); loaded directly into pre-chamber for fixed-dose arm
reagents.hoechst: 1 uM Hoechst 33342; nuclear tracking during live-cell imaging
reagents.trypsin: TrypLE (Gibco); cell detachment for retrieval (~10 s flow, ~60 s incubation)
reagents.pbs: Gibco; retrieval wash and channel flush
reagents.lysis_buffer: 10 uL ice-cold; 0.1% Triton-X-100 + RNase inhibitor (Takara); cells collected as ~2 uL droplet
reagents.cy5_tracer: Cyanine 5 (Cy5); used to characterise gradient formation kinetics (Fig. 2C)
reagents.smartseq2_reagents: Reverse transcription and pre-amplification per Picelli et al. 2014 pipeline

qpcr_genes.Tnfaip3_A20: Early NF-kB target gene; fast degradation; peaks 60 min (near) / 120 min (mid/far)
qpcr_genes.Casp4: Late NF-kB target gene; slow degradation; peaks 4-6 h; similar magnitude across positions
qpcr_genes.Ccl5_RANTES: Late NF-kB target gene; slow degradation; gradual rise; highest at mid in macrophage arm

steps.name: Chamber coating with fibronectin
steps.notes: Fibronectin loaded through inlet channels into 192 receiving chambers; incubated 30 min at RT; washed with fresh DMEM to remove unbound fibronectin before cell loading

steps.name: RelA-DsRed 3T3 fibroblast loading into receiving chambers
steps.suspension_buffer: DMEM high glucose + 10% FBS + 2 mM GlutaMAX + 1% pen/strep
steps.operation: flow-through cell loading channel (abstracted as mix in BioScript)
steps.notes: Loaded at ~70% confluency for sufficient single-cell data without significant overlap; 5 h adhesion at 37 C / 5% CO2 (midpoint of 4-6 h window)

steps.name: Hoechst 33342 nuclear staining (optional)
steps.notes: Performed selectively for nucleus tracking in live-cell epifluorescence imaging; 10 min at 37 C

steps.name: RelA-GFP RAW264.7 macrophage loading into pre-chamber
steps.operation: flow through source channel into pre-chamber (separator valve CLOSED)
steps.notes: Separator valve between pre-chamber and receiving chamber remains closed during loading; macrophages allowed to settle 30 min at 37 C before LPS stimulation

steps.name: LPS stimulation of macrophages and pre-chamber wash
steps.operation: mix (valve-directed flow into pre-chamber, separator CLOSED)
steps.wash: Fresh DMEM flowed through pre-chamber after LPS removal
steps.notes: LPS activates canonical NF-kB in RAW macrophages via TLR4; macrophages secrete TNF-a and other cytokines; LPS washed out before separator opens to prevent direct fibroblast LPS exposure

steps.name: Separator valve opening and cytokine gradient formation
steps.operation: open separator valve + initiate peristaltic sink pumping

gradient_kinetics.cy5_characterisation: Fig. 2C; heatmap shows spatial fluorescence decay from source to sink over time

steps.notes: Sink channel flushed by peristaltic pumping establishes and maintains diffusion gradient; mimics capillary clearance. Cy5 used as surrogate tracer for gradient QC; BioScript encodes as mix abstraction of valve-directed flow.

steps.name: Live-cell NF-kB translocation imaging
steps.operation: continuous epifluorescence imaging + peristaltic sink flow
steps.quantification: Nucleus/cytosol RelA-DsRed ratio per 3T3 cell; RelA-GFP tracked in RAW macrophages

findings.signaling_range: Scales with macrophage number (Fig. 3B); buffered at high densities (~60 cells)
findings.fibroblast_heterogeneity: Wide variability in response dynamics even at matched macrophage count (~60)
findings.distance_dependence: Near cells: rapid strong NF-kB activation then rapid decay; far cells: slower, lower amplitude, more heterogeneous oscillations

steps.name: Spatially resolved cell retrieval (near / mid / far)
steps.storage_encoded_in_ir: 4.0CELSIUS @ 57600.0SECOND (heat at 4c for 960m in .bs; biological intent is -80 C long-term cryostorage; compiler cannot represent negative temperatures)
steps.procedure: TrypLE flowed 10 s; partitioning valves closed before full detachment; 60 s further incubation; PBS rapidly flowed through retrieval side channels to flush cells to outlet; collected as ~2 uL droplet; deposited into ice-cold lysis buffer; stored at -80 C

steps.name: Downstream qPCR gene expression quantification
steps.pipeline: SmartSeq2: reverse transcription + pre-amplification (Picelli et al., 2014); then qPCR
steps.normalization: Each gene level normalized to maximum across all samples
steps.simulation: NF-kB translocation dynamics used as input to ODE gene expression model; degradation rate varied 20-fold to explain distance-dependent patterns (Fig. 4C)
steps.notes: Lysates stored at -80 C until processing; suitable for qPCR or RNA sequencing

supplemental_arm.name: Fixed-dose TNF-a stimulation (Section 3.4, Fig. 4)
supplemental_arm.rationale: Remove macrophage variability; use fixed 30 ng/mL TNF-a for reproducible distance-dependent gene expression comparison across samples
supplemental_arm.difference_from_main_arm: No macrophages loaded in pre-chamber; TNF-a loaded directly; otherwise identical fibroblast loading, gradient formation, cell retrieval, and qPCR pipeline
supplemental_arm.key_finding: Tnfaip3 peaks at 60 min (near) vs 120 min (mid/far); Ccl5 and Casp4 peak at 4-6 h with similar magnitude across all positions; degradation rate determines distance sensitivity of gene expression

cell_patterning_arm.name: Spatial distribution and density of sentinel cells (Section 3.5, Fig. 5)
cell_patterning_arm.rationale: 3 ng/mL LPS is sub-threshold for direct fibroblast activation; any fibroblast NF-kB activation is paracrine (macrophage-mediated)
cell_patterning_arm.finding: Macrophages at near position: strong fibroblast activation locally, weak at far; macrophages at mid position: more uniform population-level fibroblast response but weaker absolute activation than near-position loading

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Coating, fibroblast loading, Hoechst staining, macrophage loading, LPS stimulation, gradient formation

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(gradientSignal); sinkFlow + gradientJoin -> imagingChamber; NF-kB imaging; detect nfkbSignal

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(nfkbSignal); TrypLE detachment; near/mid/far lysate preparation; heat at 4c for 960m; detect geneExprSignal

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_9_f
basic_blocks.action: mix per-region waste -> drain(lysateWasteN, lysateWasteM, lysateWasteF)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_10_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(geneExprSignal); TNF-a arm entry: coating, fibroblast loading, tnfaChamber, imagingChamber2; detect geneExprSignal2

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_13_j
basic_blocks.content: TrypLE detachment; near/mid/far lysate preparation (TNF-a arm); heat at 4c for 960m; detect geneExprSignal3

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_15_f
basic_blocks.action: mix per-region waste -> drain(lysateWasteN2, lysateWasteM2, lysateWasteF2)

compiler_notes.duration_units: BioScript supports s and m only; all durations in m converted to s by compiler

duration_table.960m: 57600 s  (lysate staging; biological intent: -80 C cryostorage)

v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.fix: Replace `heat at -80c` with `heat at 4c for 960m`; biological intent (-80 C) noted in .bs comment

v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.issue: False branches emitted dispose() instead of drain()
v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.fix: Explicit waste variable in false branch; compiler emits correct dispose on waste rather than on source variable

v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.issue: Dead variable lysisBufferStock dispensed but never consumed
v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.fix: Remove standalone lysisBufferStock dispense; per-region lysis variables sufficient

v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.issue: Self-mix in imagingChamber (same variable both operands)
v1_bugs_fixed_in_v2.fix: Two distinct FreshMedium dispenses: sinkFlow and gradientJoin

compiler_notes.remaining_limitation: drain() has no dedicated opcode in lilott8/BioScript IR; all drain() calls compile to dispose() on the waste variable. The waste variable pattern (FIX2) preserves semantic intent in .bs source even though IR output is structurally identical to dispose.
